cues.en: In our next section, we'll cover neighborhood-based collaborative filtering.
cues.zh: 下一節會介紹鄰域式協同過濾。

cues.en: This is the idea of leveraging the behavior of others to inform what you might enjoy.
cues.zh: 概念是利用其他人的行為，推測你可能喜歡什麼。

cues.en: At a very high level, it means finding other people like you and recommending stuff they liked.
cues.zh: 從很高的層次來說，就是找出與你相似的人，推薦他們喜歡的東西。

cues.en: Or it might mean finding other things similar to the thing that you like.
cues.zh: 也可能是找出與你喜歡的東西相似的其他項目。

cues.en: That is, recommending stuff people bought who also bought the stuff that you liked.
cues.zh: 也就是，那些也買了你喜歡東西的人，還買了哪些東西，就推薦那些。

cues.en: Either way, the idea is taking cues from people like you, your neighborhood if you will, and recommending stuff based on the things they like that you haven't seen yet.
cues.zh: 不管哪一種，都是參考與你相似的人，也就是你的鄰域，根據他們喜歡、但你還沒看過的東西進行推薦。

cues.en: That's why we call it collaborative filtering.
cues.zh: 所以叫做協同過濾。

cues.en: It's recommending stuff based on other people's collaborative behavior.
cues.zh: 它是根據其他人的共同行為推薦。

cues.en: We're going to start off by revisiting the first architecture for top-N recommender systems we covered earlier in the course.
cues.zh: 先回顧課程前面介紹的第一種 Top-N 推薦架構。

cues.en: The way we initially did collaborative filtering at Amazon was like this.
cues.zh: 我們最初在 Amazon 做協同過濾，就是這樣。

cues.en: You start with a data store of some sort that includes rating information, be they implicit or explicit, from your users.
cues.zh: 先有某種資料儲存系統，包含使用者的隱含或明確評分資訊。

cues.en: You then generate candidates for things to recommend by looking up other items similar to the items each user liked.
cues.zh: 再查詢與每位使用者喜愛項目相似的其他項目，產生推薦候選。

cues.en: Next you score and rank those candidates, filter out the stuff the user hasn't already seen, and produce your final top-N recommendation list.
cues.zh: 接著為候選評分、排序，過濾使用者尚未看過的東西，產生最後的 Top-N 推薦清單。

cues.en: You can see the heart of this approach is really in that database of item similarities.
cues.zh: 可以看到，方法的核心就在項目相似度資料庫。

cues.en: In other approaches, you might be using a database of similarities between users instead, but either way, producing those lists of similar items or similar people is at the heart of the problem.
cues.zh: 其他方法可能改用使用者相似度資料庫；但無論哪種，產生相似項目或相似使用者清單，都是問題核心。

cues.en: So let's spend some time talking about some different ways to measure similarity between people or things.
cues.zh: 所以，花點時間談談，衡量人或物之間相似度的不同方法。

cues.en: The heart of neighborhood-based collaborative filtering is the ability to find people similar to you or items similar to items you've liked.
cues.zh: 鄰域式協同過濾的核心，是找出與你相似的人，或與你喜歡的項目相似的其他項目。

cues.en: So just like we measured the similarity between movies with content-based filtering, we can apply the same techniques to measuring similarity based on behavior data.
cues.zh: 因此，就像內容式過濾中衡量電影相似度，也能用相同技術，衡量行為資料的相似度。

cues.en: The first step in collaborative filtering is measuring the similarity between things, like these apples, or the similarity between people so you can find people like you.
cues.zh: 協同過濾第一步，是衡量物品之間的相似度，例如這些蘋果，或衡量人之間的相似度，找出與你相似的人。

cues.en: There are lots of ways to do this.
cues.zh: 有很多方法。

cues.en: The cosine similarity metric works really well in most cases.
cues.zh: 餘弦相似度在大部分情況都很好用。

cues.en: To recap, if you have a bunch of attributes associated with people or things, you can think of each attribute as a dimension and think of similarity as the angle between different things when plotted
cues.zh: 回顧一下，如果人或物有一組屬性，可以把每個屬性當成一個維度，將它們畫在

cues.en: in this multidimensional space.
cues.zh: 多維空間，再用夾角思考相似度。

cues.en: Computing the cosine of the angle turns out to be pretty straightforward, even if it's not an easy thing to visualize.
cues.zh: 即使不容易視覺化，計算角度的餘弦，卻相當直接。

cues.en: The only difference between this and when we did it with content attributes is that our dimensions will be things like, Did this user like this thing?
cues.zh: 這與前面內容屬性的唯一差異，是維度改成像這樣：這位使用者喜歡這個項目嗎？

cues.en: Or was this thing liked by this user?
cues.zh: 或這個項目受到這位使用者喜愛嗎？

cues.en: So every user or every thing might constitute its own dimension, and the dimensions are based on user behavior instead of content attributes.
cues.zh: 因此，每位使用者或每個項目，都可能成為獨立維度，維度根據使用者行為，而不是內容屬性。

cues.en: The big challenge in measuring these similarities based on the behavior data is the sparsity of the data we're working with.
cues.zh: 以行為資料衡量相似度，最大的挑戰是資料稀疏。

cues.en: There are so many movies in the world that it's very unlikely that an individual person has seen any specific movie.
cues.zh: 世界上的電影太多，某個人看過某部特定電影的機率，其實很低。

cues.en: Nobody has seen them all.
cues.zh: 沒有人看過全部電影。

cues.en: Well, my old boss at IMDB has, but he's definitely an outlier.
cues.zh: 好吧，我以前 IMDb 的老闆看過，但他絕對是極端例外。

cues.en: For the most, the data we're working with is very sparse.
cues.zh: 大部分情況，我們使用的資料非常稀疏。

cues.en: Most movies haven't been watched by a given individual.
cues.zh: 大部分電影，某位使用者都沒看過。

cues.en: And conversely, most people haven't seen a given movie, generally speaking.
cues.zh: 反過來說，一般而言，大部分人都沒看過某部特定電影。

cues.en: This means that it's tough for collaborative filtering to work well unless you have a lot of user behavior data to work with.
cues.zh: 這表示，除非有大量使用者行為資料，協同過濾很難有好效果。

cues.en: You can't compute a meaningful cosine similarity between two people when they have nothing in common, or between two items when they have no people in common.
cues.zh: 兩個人完全沒有共通項目，或兩個項目沒有共同使用者時，無法計算有意義的餘弦相似度。

cues.en: Here's an example of the data a collaborative filtering algorithm might try to be working with.
cues.zh: 這是協同過濾演算法可能會處理的資料範例。

cues.en: We usually start with a 2-D matrix like this of things, people, and the ratings that exist between them.
cues.zh: 通常從這種二維矩陣開始，包含項目、使用者，以及他們之間存在的評分。

cues.en: The problem is that matrix is mostly empty in practice.
cues.zh: 問題是，實務上矩陣大部分是空的。

cues.en: Of the four movies we listed in this example, Bob has only seen one of them, Alice has only seen one, and Ted hasn't seen any of them.
cues.zh: 例子列出的四部電影中，Bob 只看過一部，Alice 只看過一部，Ted 一部都沒看過。

cues.en: There just isn't enough data to work with, which is why we say the data is sparse.
cues.zh: 根本沒有足夠資料，所以說資料是稀疏的。

cues.en: How can I really say anything about how similar Ted is to Alice?
cues.zh: 我怎麼能判斷 Ted 與 Alice 有多相似？

cues.en: All I know is that Alice loved The Incredibles and Ted hasn't seen it for whatever reason.
cues.zh: 只知道 Alice 喜歡《超人特攻隊》，Ted 卻不知什麼原因沒看過。

cues.en: How can I say anything about the similarity between Star Wars and Casablanca?
cues.zh: 又怎麼能判斷《星際大戰》與《北非諜影》的相似度？

cues.en: I literally have no data at all on that.
cues.zh: 我真的完全沒有相關資料。

cues.en: These are the problems sparse data presents.
cues.zh: 這就是稀疏資料帶來的問題。

cues.en: This is why collaborative filtering works well for big companies like Amazon and Netflix.
cues.zh: 因此，協同過濾很適合 Amazon、Netflix 這類大公司。

cues.en: They have millions of users, and so they have enough data to generate meaningful relations in spite of the data sparsity.
cues.zh: 它們有數百萬使用者，因此儘管資料稀疏，仍有足夠資料產生有意義的關係。

cues.en: But even for our examples in this course, the 100,000 ratings we're working with aren't enough to generate really good similarity data.
cues.zh: 但即使本課程範例使用 100,000 筆評分，也不足以產生真正很好的相似度資料。

cues.en: Sparsity also introduces some computational challenges.
cues.zh: 稀疏性也帶來一些運算挑戰。

cues.en: You don't want to waste time storing and processing all of that missing data, so under the hood we end up using structures like sparse arrays that avoid storing all that empty space in this matrix.
cues.zh: 不想浪費時間儲存、處理所有缺失資料，因此內部會使用稀疏陣列等結構，避免儲存矩陣中的空白空間。

cues.en: It's just a reminder that the quantity and quality of the data that you have to work with is often way more important than the algorithm that you choose.
cues.zh: 這提醒我們，能使用的資料數量與品質，往往比選擇的演算法重要得多。

cues.en: It doesn't really matter what method you use to measure similarity if you don't have enough data to begin with.
cues.zh: 如果一開始就沒有足夠資料，用什麼方法衡量相似度，其實都沒差。

cues.en: But let's assume that you do and talk about some alternative similarity measurements that you might use.
cues.zh: 但先假設有足夠資料，再談談其他可用的相似度衡量方式。
